riskReasons: The accepted name, supported taxon and coral-stem identity are consistent across two strong institutional profiles.
Spring emergence wording differs modestly between sources and is preserved rather than forced into one exact colour.
No serious synonym or duplicate conflict was found.

duplicateCheck.notes: Compared with all RC-001–RC-010 records and all other approved Catalogue assignments. It is distinct from RC-003 ‘Sango-kaku’: RHS explicitly calls it similar, but the accepted name, published size and foliage sequence remain separate. It is also distinct from CUL-000018 ‘Aoyagi’ and CUL-000024 ‘Arakawa’. C0 resolves as unique.

identityNotes: The Atlas uses the RHS accepted hyphenated form ‘Beni-kawa’. Spaced forms are retained for search only. No synonym is approved. Coral-red young stems are a descriptive trait, not proof of identity.

content.summary: A compact to medium coral-bark Japanese maple with vivid red young stems in winter, green summer foliage and a yellow to golden autumn display.
content.habit: Bushy, spreading-branched to upright-rounded deciduous small tree. It is often relatively compact in its first decade and broadens with age.
content.leafForm: Palmate leaves with five to seven slender, pointed lobes and serrated margins. The foliage is not dissected; the main distinguishing emphasis is the combination of young-stem colour and seasonal leaves.

seasonal.spring: RHS reports pinkish-yellow opening leaves, while Missouri Botanical Garden describes soft-green emergence; small reddish flowers may occur.
seasonal.summer: Leaves mature green while young stems retain the cultivar's coral-red interest most strongly outside the leafy season.
seasonal.autumn: Foliage turns yellow to golden yellow, with source and site variation.

size.qualifier: RHS gives 2.5–4 m; Missouri Botanical Garden gives eventual dimensions of 12–15 ft, with about 5–7 ft reported over the first ten years.

content.cultivation: Provide moist, well-drained soil and a sheltered site in full sun to partial shade. In hotter climates, partial shade and consistent soil moisture reduce scorch; avoid persistently dry or exposed locations.
content.diagnostic: The comparison with RC-003 ‘Sango-kaku’ is deliberate: both have coral-toned young stems, but ‘Beni-kawa’ is maintained as a separate accepted cultivar with a generally smaller published framework and its own foliage sequence. Bark colour alone cannot authenticate either cultivar.
content.confidence: High confidence in accepted name, taxon, young-stem colour and broad habit; moderate confidence in exact spring emergence colour and mature dimensions because the two institutional profiles use different descriptions and timeframes.
content.unresolvedIssue: The pinkish-yellow versus soft-green spring-emergence wording remains source-specific, and the lean profile does not investigate original selection history.
